summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR440 crores, but EBITDA was still a negative INR15 crores (-3.4% margin) and PAT was INR2 crores.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew over 58% YoY to INR440 crores and about 16% QoQ from INR378 crores, with gross profit up 64% YoY to INR34 crores. Gross margin improved to 7.8% from 7.3% in Q4 FY26, and EBITDA loss narrowed to INR15 crores from INR20 crores. PAT of INR2 crores compared with a loss of INR13 crores in Q4 FY26 but remained below the INR26 crores reported in Q1 FY26. Management said July revenue was about INR150 crores (subject to audit) and that it does not expect EBITDA positivity for the next two to three years at group level.

financial_highlights.metric: July FY27 revenue (monthly ARR, subject to audit)

segments.name: RetailerShakti
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 48% YoY and remains the principal growth engine; gross margin about 7.8% and EBITDA close to break-even, with management targeting positive EBITDA in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: SastaSundar (B2C via Health Buddy franchisees)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 44% YoY; management attributes about 90% of its EBITDA loss to technology build-up and says the model spends about 15% of revenue on building it. Segment P&L is not disclosed.

segments.name: JITO private label
segments.commentary: Sales rose from about INR25 lakhs in Q4 FY26 to about INR79 lakhs in Q1 FY27 (about 200% growth), with gross margin said to be above 50%; still a very small share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Entire FY27 gross margin to be maintained at 8% plus; medium-term industry gross margin of about 12% cited as target.
RetailerShakti expected to reach positive EBITDA in Q3 FY27.
Management described FY27 as possibly the best year in company history, with Q1 as the best quarter ever; no formal annual revenue guidance given.
Company not expected to be EBITDA positive for the next two to three years; focus stated as cash flow and capital efficiency.
RetailAir AI-monitored SaaS for retailers scheduled to launch in Q2 FY27.
Existing plus side-extension fulfilment capacity said to support revenue up to about INR3,000 crores; existing capacity described as running at about 90%.
capex_capacity: New warehouses: Noida operational (new facility starting 17 August); West Bengal partly done; Guwahati 75,000 sq ft rented, owned construction to start in about 6 months.
Udaipur construction started; Patna and Lucknow to start in about 2-3 months; Ranchi warehouse planned in Jharkhand.
Management says it intends to own fulfilment infrastructure rather than rely on third-party warehouses; no capex quantum disclosed.
JITO conversions: 19 Health Buddies converted to JITO, 25 in pipeline; about 50% of Health Buddies expected to convert within 3 months.
demand_pricing: Customer base: about 75,000 retail pharmacies served, 40,000 active in last 30 days; average wallet share about 2%.
Order-size mix: 69.4% of RetailerShakti business from orders above INR2,500 and 42.4% above INR5,000; 69.2% of SastaSundar orders above INR1,000.

Geography: about 67% of RetailerShakti and 78% of SastaSundar business from tier 2 and tier 3 markets; West Bengal share about 70% per analyst question, with management citing about 30% now from West Bengal in the call.
Expansion into Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, UP, Rajasthan; Northeast cited as the fastest-growing region.
Sourcing: over 95% of purchases direct from pharma companies; purchase returns below 1%; more than 50,000 SKUs from over 1,000 vendors.
Management estimates current market share in Kolkata and West Bengal at about 3-4%, with a target of about 7% in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are gross and EBITDA margins for RetailerShakti in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin about 7.8%; EBITDA close to break-even, with positive EBITDA expected in Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 revenue aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give annual projections; July revenue was above INR150 crores (subject to audit), which it said investors can extrapolate.

qa_highlights.question: How will gross margin ramp, and what is the JITO contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects blended B2B and B2C gross margin to move toward about 12%, driven by volume, wallet share and private label; it declined to give a JITO share target but said internal projections exceed analyst scenarios of 5-6% of revenue within three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SastaSundar burn and its split?
qa_highlights.answer: Lokesh Agarwal put the burn at about 25-30% marketing and advertising and 40-45% technology; management said segment P&L is not yet separable because procurement, fulfilment and tech are integrated.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the EBITDA break-even timeline moved from one or two years to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied any postponement, saying RetailerShakti is near break-even and that break-even at group level was never promised for the current year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the warehouse and fulfilment capacity status?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing infrastructure can handle about 100% growth from current levels (INR2,500-3,000 crores), with existing plus side extensions sufficient up to about INR3,000 crores revenue; company operates last-mile riders on its own payroll.

risks_watch: SastaSundar burn (technology and marketing) continues with no segment disclosure; management said segment P&L carve-out is in progress with no timeline.
PAT of INR2 crores is below Q1 FY26 INR26 crores; EBITDA still negative at INR15 crores.
Gross margin of 7.8% is below management's 8%-plus full-year target and far below the 12% industry benchmark it cited.
Treasury income cited as a source of 7-8% of revenue; in response to a question, management confirmed it as treasury income, so core operating revenue quality is a question.
Pending SEBI approval for the merger and demerger scheme; management said it is on track and that stock exchange queries are being answered.
Check RetailAir launch in Q2 FY27 and whether the claimed working-capital and inventory benefits materialise.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, JITO and the long-term model, but evasive on specifics such as segment burn, SastaSundar losses, and quantitative JITO targets. Management repeatedly deflected EBITDA questions toward cash flow and capital efficiency.
key_quotes: So July, we ended with INR150 crores plus revenue.
We are not an EBITDA positive company for the next two, three years and we neither look the EBITDA from perspective.
This quarter is the best quarter in the history of the company.
So we have estimated that if we say build a INR2,000 crores SastaSundar company then we spend 15% of that INR300 crores.
So, we will not stop our investment in technology, maybe more and more, so -- but definitely we will disclose it appropriately.
